memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The priest is to go outside the camp and examine them. If they have been healed of their defiling skin disease, the priest shall order that two live clean birds and some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop be brought for the person to be cleansed." - Lev 14:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read the first line slowly. The priest is to go outside the camp.

The unclean person could not come in. So the priest went out. He left the place of worship, left the safety and the community, and walked to where the excluded one was waiting. He went to them.

That single detail is the shape of the whole gospel. We could not come to God. So God came to us. The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us (John 1:14). Jesus did not stand at the edge of the camp calling for people to clean themselves up and approach. He came out.

And He kept going out. Out to the tax collectors' tables. Out to the Samaritan woman at the well. Out to the demon-possessed man in the tombs whom the whole town had given up on. And finally, all the way out — He suffered outside the city gate (Heb 13:12), dying in the place of the excluded, so the excluded could come home.

Whatever "outside the camp" means for you — the shame you assume disqualifies you, the distance you feel from God, the room you think you cannot enter — He knows the way there. He has walked it before.

He is not waiting for you to arrive. He has already come out to meet you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you feel too far outside for God to come?
2. What does it change to know Jesus moves towards you first?
3. Who is "outside the camp" in your world that you could go to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You did not wait for me to reach You but came out to where I was. Thank You for going outside the gate for me. Make me someone who goes out to others. Amen.
